transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 min
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Nguyen (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (CTO, Evergreen Clinic), Liam Chen (IT Manager), Priya Singh (Compliance)

Summary: Walkthrough of Redwood rate-limiting, org vs project keys, quotas, and multi-tenant controls. Demo of Console flows (org/project key creation, per-project quotas, alerts), and discussion of pilot scope and security/compliance needs. Agreed next steps: pricing + docs from AE, initial POC/benchmarks with SE.

Topics: rate limits, quotas, org/project keys, per-route limits, burst capacity, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, SOC 2/KMS, pilot benchmarks.

Quick links referenced: https://redwood.ai/docs/rate-limits (demo guide), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf (security pack)

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time 
- Samir from Redwood here, AE on this account. Quick intros?
[00:15] Maya: Hi, Maya Rodriguez, CTO at Evergreen Clinic. I'm joined by Liam and Priya.
[00:20] Liam: Liam Chen, I manage infra and integrations.
[00:22] Priya: Priya Singh, compliance.
[00:25] Samir: Great. Jules from our SE team will run the demo, I'll handle pricing/contract questions.
[00:35] Jules: Hi all; I'll jump into the console and show how we do org keys vs project keys and the rate limiting controls. Quick note: transcription may have a few typos, you'll see things like KV cahce in older docs, ha.
[01:12] Samir: Quick qual question before we dive 
- what's your current usage pattern? average qps, peaks, and any regulatory constraints?
[01:25] Maya: For production we expect ~30 qps average for our triage assistant, peaking to maybe 120 qps during clinic hours. Data residency: patient PII can't leave the region, so VPC or private deployment is preferred.
[01:40] Liam: Also latency targets are important 
- sub 300ms for short text completions is the goal. Cost is also a big factor; we need predictable spending.
[01:55] Samir: Makes sense. We'll look at dedicated or private options for residency; Hosted API can still be used with VPC peering for certain regions but we'll detail options.
[02:05] Jules: ok jumping into screen share, console home 
- you can see the org overview, and under Security > API Keys we have Org keys and Project keys. Org keys are for cross-project admin tooling, project keys are scoped and have quotas.
[02:40] Jules: (narrating) Here I'm creating a project key for 'triage-assistant' 
- we can set per-key rate limits: requests per minute, tokens per minute, and also enforcement mode (soft warn vs hard block).
[03:00] Maya: Can we do per-route limits too? Like limit generation routes separately from embedding calls?
[03:10] Jules: Yes 
- per-route and even per-model limits. You can set a quota for text-generation route differently than embeddings. We also surface token-level cost breakdowns per key in the console.
[03:40] Priya: How do you handle burst capacity? Some days we get sudden spikes when the appointment reminder batch runs.
[03:50] Jules: We have burst policies 
- you define baseline quota and burst allowance. For higher SLA you can use Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) which guarantees throughput; hosted has autoscaling but less predictable tail latency during extreme bursts.
[04:20] Liam: So for dedicated, is that reserved GPUs with a monthly commit? and does rate limiting still apply?
[04:30] Samir: Yes, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools 
- rate limits are still enforced at the org/project layer, but you get predictable throughput and lower chance of throttling. We can also set separate limits per deployment group.
[05:00] Jules: On the console I'll also show alerts 
- you can add an alert that fires when a project hits 80% of its token quota or when error rates spike. Alerts can notify Slack, webhook, email.
[05:20] Maya: About the keys themselves 
- we want to restrict use so that only certain services can call high-privileged endpoints. Can you do role-based key policies?
[05:30] Jules: We have RBAC in the control plane 
- keys map to projects and you can scope by role; for example, create a read-only ingestion key vs a full generate key. We integrate with SSO / SAML so user provisioning maps to project roles.
[06:10] Priya: On encryption 
- we need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Is that supported?
[06:20] Samir: Yes, KMS integration is standard for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key for certain enterprise plans. We'll share the SOC2 and KMS docs after this call.
[06:50] Jules: small note 
- some of the older docs say "KV cache" as "K V cache" in transcriptions; ignore that, but we do prefix/KV caching to speed up repeated prompts and save tokens.
[07:10] Liam: Do quotas consider cached tokens or only new generation?
[07:20] Jules: By default quota charges on generated tokens; prefix/KV cahce hits may reduce billed tokens because generation is shorter. We can show estimates during the POC.
[07:45] Maya: Can we throttle per customer ID within a single project? we have multitenant app where each clinic location is a tenant 
- we want per-tenant controls.
[07:55] Jules: Two ways: you can create project keys per tenant, or use per-caller metadata + rate-limiting rules that inspect headers. Our routing layer supports request-level policies. There's also a middleware pattern for usage attribution.
[08:30] Samir: If you want to avoid creating thousands of keys, projects + per-caller rules usually work better; but keys give strong isolation for billing.
[09:00] Maya: What's the UX for rotating keys? we need regular rotation policy for security.
[09:10] Jules: Keys can be rotated in the console 
- create new key, swap, revoke old. We also have short-lived session keys via our token broker for services.
[09:30] Liam: On the API side, how do we pass project metadata? in headers?
[09:35] Jules: Yes, header-based or query param (header preferred). Example: x-redwood-project: triage-assistant. The request attributes are visible in logs for billing and audit.
[10:05] Priya: Audit logs availability? we need immutable logs for compliance.
[10:10] Samir: Audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private with configurable retention. For Hosted we have tiered retention add-ons. We'll include retention table in the security pack.
[10:40] Jules: Back to quotas 
- you can do hard quotas (reject requests) or soft quotas (throttle to lower rate) and also set token or request-based budgets. In console you can configure daily, monthly, or rolling 30-day quotas.
[11:15] Maya: Can quotas be per-model variant? e.g., restrict a high-cost (large) model to lower traffic while allowing smaller models for general use.
[11:25] Jules: Absolutely 
- you can set model profiles and enforce quotas per-model. We also provide recommender suggestions in Redwood Optimize that suggest quantization or smaller model variants for certain routes to cut costs.
[12:00] Liam: About billing 
- is it per-token even for embeddings? and do quotas map to billing units?
[12:10] Samir: Embeddings are billed per-embedding unit; quotas can map to tokens or embedding units depending on route. We'll show mapping in the pricing sheet.
[12:40] Maya: Show us a sample policy for an org with 10 clinics and a shared triage project.
[12:50] Jules: (switches to policy editor) Here's a policy: baseline project quota 1M tokens/day, per-tenant rule: max 200k tokens/day per tenant, burst allowance 2x for 2 minutes. Enforcement actions are set to soft-warn first then hard block if sustained.
[13:30] Maya: If we do hard block, can requests failover to a fallback model or degrade gracefully?
[13:40] Jules: Yes, we have routing fallbacks 
- automatic fallback to smaller model or alternate region. You can also configure A/B or canary rollouts to test.
[14:05] Priya: Any PII filters or processors before data leaves our VPC?
[14:15] Jules: For Private deployments, you control the networking so data never leaves. For Hosted there's optional pre-processing hooks and PII redactors. We'll share details.
[14:45] Liam: On the SE benchmark side 
- can you simulate our traffic pattern? we have spikes around 8am and 5pm, plus batch jobs at 02:00.
[14:55] Jules: Yes, for POC we can replay traces or synthetic load. We'll need a sample trace, token distributions, and preferred models.
[15:30] Samir: Pricing aside 
- one common tradeoff is throughput vs cost. We typically recommend dedicated for predictable high throughput, hosted for lower ops overhead. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/quantization to save up to 40% token cost on sample workloads.
[16:10] Maya: Any hard limits on number of projects or keys?
[16:20] Jules: No hard limit 
- but for orgs with thousands of projects we recommend using hierarchical org keys and automation for lifecycle.
[16:45] Priya: About SAML/SCIM provisioning 
- do you support group-based role assignment?
[16:55] Samir: Yes, SSO + SCIM mapping to Redwood roles is supported; we have examples for Okta, Azure AD in the security pack.
[17:20] Liam: How do we measure token usage per feature? we want breakdown so product can decide where to optimize.
[17:30] Jules: Per-route token dashboards, per-key breakdown, and token-level cost charts. You can also export CSV or connect to our metrics API.
[18:05] Maya: Is there rate limiting at network edge too? like per-IP?
[18:15] Jules: Yes, edge-level protections, and WAF integration. You can block or rate-limit on IP, ASN, or geolocation.
[18:45] Samir: Quick interjection 
- competitors sometimes have opaque throttling behaviors. We pride ourselves on explicit SLOs and transparent quotas.
[19:05] Maya: Ok good. For the pilot, we want a week-long POC with latency and cost numbers and a security review.
[19:15] Samir: Sounds good. We'll scope the POC: goals are 1) average latency under 300ms for baseline load; 2) cost per 1k tokens estimate vs current; 3) policy testing for per-tenant quotas.
[19:45] Jules: For the benchmark I'll need a sample of your prompt sizes and a representative traffic trace. If you can drop that in the shared folder we'll start.
[20:05] Maya: We'll share that 
- Priya will also attach compliance doc.
[20:20] Priya: I'll send the compliance checklist and regs list.
[20:35] Samir: Great, I'll email the pricing + org/project keys one-pager and the security pack (SOC2 + KMS notes).
[21:00] Maya: A couple of extra Qs 
- how long does security review usually take?
[21:10] Priya: (asks) do you have standard questionnaires?
[21:20] Samir: Typical security review is 2-4 weeks for full enterprise pack; we have a standard security questionnaire and the SOC2 addendum, which we will attach.
[21:45] Priya: Great.
[22:00] Maya: Any blockers from our side to start the POC?
[22:05] Liam: We'll need an NDA in place (we have a standard one) and a brief data sheet for the test.
[22:20] Samir: We can accommodate NDA; I'll coordinate with legal.
[22:40] Jules: For the POC, I'll need to know target SLAs and model variants to test (gpt-style large vs quantized small).
[23:00] Maya: We'll default to our current model pairing, but open to recommendations.
[23:20] Samir: Redwood Optimize can propose smaller/quantized models to reduce cost 
- we'll include sample recommendations.
[23:50] Priya: One more compliance Q 
- does Redwood offer isolated logging for audit review?
[24:00] Samir: Yes, isolated audit streams for customers, with configurable retention.
[24:30] Jules: Also note session-level logs are redacted for PII unless you explicitly allow raw logs in private deployments.
[25:00] Maya: Great. Anything else?
[25:10] Liam: I have a minor question about token accounting for prompt engineering 
- if we use prefix caching heavily, how do we attribute cost per tenant?
[25:20] Jules: We can attribute based on final generation tokens; prefix caching reduces generation length but attribution can be customized in the billing rules. We'll show this in the POC.
[26:00] Samir: Alright we'll send the pricing doc and security pack. Expected follow-up email by tomorrow with attachments.
[26:15] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[26:20] Priya: Thanks.
[26:25] Jules: Thanks all, talk soon.

(Transcript ends 
- meeting length ~45 minutes; some timestamps abbreviated in transcription.)
